notes.title: Major Update
notes.content:
[h2]Upgrade to version 1.2.1[/h2]

- better rendering pipeline, which improves performance and increases capabilities
- improved visuals and lighting throughout the game with post processing 
- One excessively large level (Ancient Ruins, Old King's Castle, and the Hidden Tomb) was split into 2 separate levels and significantly redesigned for significant performance increases.  It was too big as one giant level, took up too much memory, and I don't have the resources to manage that properly yet.
- Improved level and environmental design in most open areas with new procedural instancing features and higher quality props
- New save point pillar located in cathedral road at an abandoned hut.  This should help provide some relief while exploring this massive open forest area
- Enemies and items may have moved it the redesigned areas, but the same items plus more available find in the world. 
[b]- Save file integrity should remain with this update, but please contact me with any issues.  Players who have progressed far enough in the previously mentioned areas on a saved game may notice duplicates of spawn locations listed in their fast travel menu. This can be ignored and should not happen in new game.[/b]

[h2]Additional Changes and Notes:[/h2]

- another round of sound effects balancing and fixes. more to come in the near future
- home screen theme music changed to a better quality soundtrack
- background music added to the sanctuary to give a more tranquil but melancholy feeling
- more tool tips added to the loading screen, and they can be iterated through by pressing A (xbox controller layout) on a gamepad or space on the keyboard 
- when in game and choosing and item to equip in the inventory screen, all items that don't match the chosen slot's equipment type are now greyed out in the inventory contents panel (this actually made it into the last update and I think I forgot to mention it, so it's been live for awhile now)
- weapons that are equipped but you do not have the proper stats to wield them now show a red 'X' over their icon/slot in the equipment panel of the inventory menu.  Check item info for stat requirements. [b]Wielding a weapon without the proper stats results in very slow animation speeds, significantly decreased damage outputs, and spells won't be cast.[/b]
-  Cutscenes can be skipped by either pressing Escape on the keyboard, or pressing B (xbox controller layout) on a gamepad to enable a notification sign "Skip" to appear on screen.  Press the same button again before the sign disappears to skip the cutscene.  This has been in the live version for quite some time, but I noticed several content creators didn't know they could do this.  It is currently a tool tip on the loading screen, but due to the amount of tooltips and the random nature of their appearance, it wasn't showing up often enough for players to see it.

Coming in the next few weeks:
- AI improvements to help avoid erratic behaviors and better decision making in combat
- More audio balance fixes and sfx replacements as needed
- a short break for me: my brain hurts and needs it... unless significant bugs are reported and need addressed ASAP

Thank you for the continued support! Current and old players may feel like they are playing a totally different world with the new designs and performance improvements.  I look forward to new players experiencing what I've created and for all to provide me with feedback on how I can make it better going forward!

As always, feel free to engage with me on the Community Hub via Steam or hop into the discord server if you have any questions, concerns, bug reports and suggestions.

Don't forget to leave a review if you've had a chance to play the game!

Thanks again,

Jerry

notes.title: Into the Future
notes.content:
[h2]Current News for Chaos[/h2]

Chaos has been a passionate project of mine for quite some time now.  With that being said, I want to see it become the game so many of you have expressed that it [i]could[/i] be, and be successful in the long run. I will continue to make improvements based on player feedback, resource and technology access, and continue learning more about game development as a whole.  I appreciate all of you who have taken the time to give Chaos a chance and play it through to the end.  Your feedback has been extremely helpful!

[h3]Current Development:[/h3]
[list]
[*]I am currently upgrading to a new rendering pipeline to take advantage of more advanced and optimized rendering technology.  This will also open new doors for other tools and techniques not previously available, and allow for easier expansion in the future.  It will take a bit of time because I'll have to recreate many custom shaders that are not compatible with the new pipeline.
[*] The upgrade above will allow for me to fill in the world with more environment details because of the increased optimization.
[*] Level/World design changes.  Once the pipeline upgrades are complete, I'll be able to reassess the world design and will hopefully be making drastic changes to make the game more interesting.
[*]  Audio improvements are in the works as well for the next update.  More balance should help improve the immersion of the game and alleviate some frustrations that players have expressed.  I am not an audio engineer, so this has been a struggle from the beginning.  Sometimes, what one person likes, others do not, so it can be a bit subjective but I will do my best to address all issues.
[/list]

[h3]Future Development:[/h3]
[list]
[*] I have plans for a large expansion in the spring of 2021 that will include a new area to explore, more enemy varieties, bosses, weapons, spells, and will hopefully introduce new mechanics to the gameplay, such as key items needed for progression.
[*] I have plans and have actually already attempted to build a multiplayer/invasion system.  It is a new world for me and will take some time, but with enough support I may be able to get some help with integration of some 3rd party assets and development.
[/list]

Thanks!

Jerry

notes.title: PlayStation and other Controller Issues
notes.content:
Hello,

I've recently had quite a few players point out some issues with various types of controllers they are trying to use.  The core game architecture fully supports XboxOne/360 controller input, and Steam handles the input mapping for all other types of recognized controllers in use, but I unknowingly had to tell it to do so.  Most of those issues should now be resolved.

If you continue to have issues, there are a few things you can try:

- Go to Steam -> Settings -> Controller -> General Controller Settings, then make sure that the box is checked next to your type of controller. 
- Right-Click on the application in your library view, select settings, and make sure "Steam Input Per-Game Setting" is set to "Use your Global Input Settings." If that doesn't work, try "Forced On."

- If the above steps don't work, try running the game in Big Picture Mode.  This has worked for some players as a first step, but I personally don't like BPM and I'm sure others do not either.

If none of these steps have resolved your issues with your controller, please let me know in the Discussion boards or send me an email and I will look further into it.

Thanks to everyone who has given Chaos a try and provided me with feedback.  I look forward to improving the game as needed and resolving any issues you are having.

Thanks!

notes.title: Routine Updates
notes.content:
[h1]I've been searching for and patiently awaiting feedback from players from all over the world who have been tearing apart the demo and I appreciate it all![/h1]

[h2][b][u]Gameplay mechanics and other Updates:[/u][/b][/h2]

- A stamina-based stat ring was added to the game to significantly reduce the cost of stamina while running

- Doors that can't be opened from one side now display an announcement that says so, making it a bit more obvious that the door is intended to be opened later in the game as a sort of short-cut.

- 1 new boss and 1 new enemy type were added to give a bit more diversity and more gameplay experiences.

- audio balancing.  more to come in the future based on feedback

- AI now includes a death broadcast mechanic that will automatically force nearby enemies to aggro to you.  You can still sneak up behind enemies for a couple free hits in some scenarios.  Other improvements to the AI to make it a bit more intuitive and responsive.

- Various animation improvements.  some placeholder animations were replaced, others will be fixed and replaced in the future.  This includes weapon placements in the hand for most weapons and spells.  More fixes to come in the near future.

- Increased text size and font style of the damage amount pop-ups on enemy UI to make it a bit more readable.

- Enemies no longer trigger a blood spatter when they hit each other to help avoid confusion and a weird visual that happens

[i]*** many other smaller QOL updates to help improve your experience.[/i]

[h2][b][u]Game Balance Changes:[/u][/b][/h2]
[i]*** Game balance is an ongoing endeavor and will continue to be improved based on player feedback, just like as in most other games. [/i] 

-  Stamina system improved.  Stamina now has a 1 second delay vs 2 seconds before regenerating, and the regeneration speed has been increased.  Exhausting your stamina completely now results in a 2 second delay penalty instead of 4 seconds.

- Wolves: now move slightly slower to allow the player to gain more distance if needed, attack damage has been reduced in certain areas where it spiked for some reason, and there is a slight windup to their bight attacks to provide a window for the player to dodge if they wish

- Weapons have been overhauled:  Too many changes to list, but it should make for a more progressive and rewarding experience.  Damage has been increased on all damage-dealing special abilities.  Keep in mind, the type of weapon determines it's overall DPS - shorter/lighter weapons swing faster, but do less base damage and have less reach than other types; halberds/staves/spears deal much less damage and have slower animations, but have much longer reach to keep distance; heavy weapons like maces/axes/greataxes deal the greatest amount of damage, but are the slowest to wield and have mid-range reach.  Each item is unique in terms of hitbox size.

- fireball spell casting time slightly reduced

- Damage output slightly reduced for the first boss to prevent one-shotting the sorcerer character.

[b][u]Next on the To-Do list:[/u][/b]

- Changes to the options menu to be a bit more intuitive when using a controller

- more animation fixes and replacements

- continued balance improvements as necessary

- better audio balancing

[b]Please continue providing me with feedback on what you think could make the game a better overall experience![/b]

notes.title: Small Update: 8/9/2020
notes.content:
[u][b]This week:[/b][/u] 

i spent time playing through the entire cemetery area checking for environment issues (such as missing collision on trees, issues with terrain slope or places where a player can escape the intended play area, structure placements, etc.), enemy behaviors, and overall feel of the game play.  In doing so, I noticed that at some point while modifying terrain I created other issues.  For example, the location of the stairs to the sanctuary became hidden from the player beneath the terrain but has since been fixed. 

[b]Fixes and Notes:[/b]

- Changes in the terrain required a new enemy path finding mesh to be baked as well.  

- Slight tweaks to enemy behavior should make them a bit more responsive.

- Updated a few UI elements, such as the quick menu buttons and background, upgrade vendor buttons and background, and a few others.

- Inventory fixes have been implemented to remove duplication of items, loss of items on transfers between inventory, equipment, and the storage box, and correct quantities being shown.

- Interaction with items in the inventory has been changed as well.  Clicking an item now presents the player with a popup menu with choices to use or drop the item, or cancel the interaction.  This is more intuitive than the previous method of operation and is more clear to the player on how to interact with the inventory.

- Lighting is continuing to be a bane to my existence and I can't seem to produce a result that I'm happy with (issues include the actual visual result, the total time it takes to bake, and memory usage).  I'm looking into alternative solutions to better present the world.

[u][b]Next week:[/b][/u]

My goals for the final weeks before launch are to complete another play through of each area myself and help pick up on any bugs that may not be caught by the testers.  I am also looking for areas that could use a little TLC as far as environment design.  I am no artist, so input certainly helps from an outside perspectives.  

Game balance (enemy health pools, damage outputs, currency collection, leveling rates, etc.) will be addressed in early September as well.

[u][b]Near Future:[/b][/u]

I am waiting for artwork so that I can include the intro and ending cutscenes in the build which will be the final additions to the game.  At this point, no new features will be added prior to release unless significant issues require a massive modification.

[i]Thank you to all who are testing the game for me - your feedback has been great and I look forward to hearing from you again soon![/i]
